card.title: Better at the System
card.instruction: Treat every rule, shortcut, and correction as a chance to prove you understand the system better than anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My parking permit took six minutes at the expedited counter. Still filling yours in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You must have found my counter. Did you mention the renewal exemption?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used the website. It applied that automatically.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you haven't learned where they hide the appeal button. I'll show you before you need it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 competes on permit speed, A3 assumes B used A's shortcut and tests an exemption, and A5 shifts to a hidden appeal feature after the website surpasses both.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's five minutes causes A3's counter-and-exemption test; B4's automated web success causes A5's new advanced-knowledge offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 provides a better result and B4 explains the actual method instead of accepting A's credit.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's website correction to find another part of that system where A can still claim superiority.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a permit application and measured completion times.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's before-you-need-it appeal offer is earned by B4's successful automated path.
